slides.title: System.IO Overview
slides.content: File operations in C# live in System.IO. The main types are File, FileStream, StreamReader, and StreamWriter for text I/O.

exercise.prompt: Which namespace contains file I/O classes?

slides.title: FileStream Basics
slides.content: FileStream provides raw byte-level access to files. You specify the path, mode, and access when creating it.
slides.example: FileStream fs = new FileStream("data.txt", FileMode.OpenOrCreate, FileAccess.ReadWrite);

exercise.prompt: To create a file if missing or open existing, use FileMode._____.

slides.title: Reading with StreamReader
slides.content: StreamReader reads characters from a file stream. ReadLine reads one line at a time until the end of the stream.

exercise.prompt: Drag the method that reads one line from a text file: sr [?]().

slides.title: Writing with StreamWriter
slides.content: StreamWriter writes characters to a file. WriteLine adds a newline after each call. The using statement ensures the file is closed.

exercise.prompt: Write a StreamWriter line to save the text 'Saved' into log.txt.
exercise.expectedOutput: Compiles with WriteLine and correct string.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: StreamWriter, WriteLine
When run, your code should output: Compiles with WriteLine and correct string.

slides.title: Reading an Entire File
slides.content: ReadToEnd returns all remaining text as a single string. It is useful for small files but can use a lot of memory.

exercise.prompt: Which method reads all text at once?

slides.title: File Modes and Access
slides.content: FileMode controls creation and opening behavior: Open, Create, Append, OpenOrCreate. FileAccess controls read, write, or read/write.
slides.example: FileStream fs = new FileStream("log.txt", FileMode.Append, FileAccess.Write);

exercise.prompt: Use FileMode._____ to add to the end of an existing file.

slides.title: Using Statements and Disposal
slides.content: StreamReader and StreamWriter implement IDisposable. The using statement automatically closes and flushes the stream.

exercise.prompt: Drag the statement that ensures a stream is closed: [?] (StreamReader sr = ...)

slides.title: File Operations Review
slides.content: Use FileStream for byte-level control and StreamReader or StreamWriter for text. Always dispose streams to release file handles.

exercise.prompt: Write a using block that opens note.txt for reading and reads one line into a variable.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: StreamReader, ReadLine
When run, your code should output: StreamReader, sr.ReadLine()
